summary: The root كَلَحَ (kalaha) describes a person who grins, showing their teeth, often with a frowning or stern facial expression.
lane: 1 كَلَحَ ذ , aor. كَلَحَ , inf. n. كُلُوحٌ and كُلَاحٌ ; (S, K;) and , and , (K,) and ; (A;) He (a man, S) grinned, or displayed his teeth, (M, rendered in the S and K by تَكَشَّرَ ), frowning, or contracting his face, or looking sternly, austerely, or morosely. (S, M, K.) -b2- كَلَحَ فِى وَجْهِهِ He frightened him; namely a child, and a madman. (A.)

headwords.gloss: He contended with him for superiority in strength; i. q

headwords.gloss: it; made him to grin; display his teeth, frowning
